newsitem.title: USA: Claudette fades in north Atlantic.
newsitem.headline: Claudette fades in north Atlantic.

text.p: Claudette faded in the north Atlantic Ocean on Tuesday and was downgraded to a tropical depression as it moved away from the U.S. coast, hurricane forecasters said.

At 5 a.m. EDT (0900 GMT), the center of Claudette was located at latitude 35.8 north, longitude 70.3 west, about 300 miles (480 km) east of Cape Hatteras, North Carolina, the National Hurricane Center said.
It was moving northeast at 12 mph (19 kph) and was expected to turn gradually toward the east.
Maximum sustained winds were 35 mph (56 kph).
Claudette, the third tropical storm of the 1997 Atlantic hurricane season, formed Sunday when its maximum winds topped 39 mph (62 kph).
Tropical depressions become tropical storms and are given names when sustained winds reach 39 mph (62 kph). Tropical storms become hurricanes when winds hit 74 mph (118 kph).
